title: Voll's Unbeaten 131 Outshines Mostary's Historic 118 as Australia Seal ODI Series
excerpt: Sobhana Mostary's record 118 — the first century by a Bangladesh woman against Australia — was eclipsed within hours as Georgia Voll's unbeaten 131 powered a nine-wicket win that sealed the series 2-0.
body:
• Georgia Voll smashed an unbeaten 131 off 97 balls to power Australia to a nine-wicket win over Bangladesh in the second ODI at Brisbane's Allan Border Field.
  • Sobhana Mostary made 118 off 134 balls — the first century by a Bangladesh woman against Australia, and the highest individual score in Bangladesh women's ODI history.
  • Mostary's 195-run fourth-wicket stand with captain Nigar Sultana (74 not out) is the highest ODI partnership ever recorded against Australia women.
  • The chase of 222 in 28.1 overs sealed the three-match series 2-0 for Australia with a game to play.

Bangladesh produced the most famous innings in their women's cricket history on Saturday night at the Allan Border Field. Australia then chased it down in 28 overs and won anyway.

Sobhana Mostary's 118 off 134 balls — the first hundred by a Bangladesh woman against Australia, and the highest score ever by a Bangladeshi woman in ODIs — dragged the tourists from 8 for 3 to 220 for 6. Hours later, Georgia Voll answered with an unbeaten 131 off 97 balls, the highest individual women's ODI score at the Brisbane venue, as Australia reached 222 for 1 with 131 balls to spare and sealed the three-match series 2-0.

"I love batting out there with Phoebe and to have a partnership and get the team off to a good start was the most important thing. I base my game off a power game — I look to hit the ball hard and straight early and take it on once I get in."

— Georgia Voll, Player of the Match

A historic rescue act

Bangladesh's innings looked finished almost before it began. Asked to bat first under lights, the tourists took 20 deliveries to score their first run off the bat, then slumped to 8 for 3 as Megan Schutt ripped through the top order, finishing with 4 for 36 from her 10 overs. Kim Garth (1 for 35) was the only other wicket-taker.

https://x.com/cricketcomau/status/2109235433217667395

What followed was the finest partnership in Bangladesh women's cricket. Mostary, 24, and captain Nigar Sultana (74 not out from 114 balls) added 195 for the fourth wicket — the highest ODI partnership ever against the Australian women, who rarely concede triple-figure stands. Mostary brought up her fifty from 66 balls before shifting gears, reaching her century off 123 deliveries with 18 boundaries. Her 118 eclipsed Fargana Hoque's previous national record of 107 and made her only the third Bangladeshi batter, across men's and women's cricket, to score an ODI century in Australia, after Mahmudullah and Tanzid Hasan Tamim.

Voll's reply: power and inevitability

Records at this venue have a way of falling fast. Voll's unbeaten 131 became the highest individual women's ODI total at Allan Border Field — breaking the mark Mostary had equalled only hours earlier — and made the 23-year-old the first woman to score two ODI centuries at the ground after her 101 against India there in 2024.

Her third ODI century in just her 15th match took only 81 balls to complete. Opening with Phoebe Litchfield (70 off 51, with 11 fours and a six), Voll put on 162 in 19.5 overs of pure dominance, 82 of them in the opening powerplay. When Shorna Akter finally broke the stand in the 20th over, Ellyse Perry (19 not out) joined Voll to complete the formality.

What it means for the series — and the rankings race

The result gives Australia an unassailable 2-0 lead, but the night belonged to Bangladesh's progress. For a side that has never beaten Australia in ODIs, producing a 195-run stand against the world's best attack is the kind of marker that changes how opponents prepare for them.

For India, watching closely from home, the series offers timely intelligence. The Women's ODI World Cup cycle continues to reward exactly the brand of batting both sides showed: Bangladesh's graft-to-attack blueprint, and Australia's relentless power game. Voll's innings in particular underlined why the world champions remain the side to beat — no total fazes them, and they chase without a second gear.

What's next

The third and final ODI gives Bangladesh a chance to turn a moral victory into a historic one. Australia, already the series winners, will look to extend their dominance — and Voll will look to keep a purple patch running that is making her one of the most feared openers in the women's game.
